title: Defibrillator safety

sources.use: ERC ALS 2025 (paraphrase only; commercial use needs ERC agreement)

objectives: Keep the pre-shock pause as short as possible.
Perform and call the safety check so nobody touches the patient or bed at the moment of shock.
Recognise authorised-role requirements and call for help.

items.text: Rhythm analysis and the decision to shock follow resuscitation policy and the authorised role; this skill does not teach rhythm interpretation or energy settings.

Before an indicated shock, call the safety warning and visually confirm that no person is in contact with the patient or bed. Never deliver a shock during manual compressions, even if gloves are worn. Follow the device and local electrical-safety pathway.
Pads are preferred over paddles when available; if paddles are used apply firm force and good contact to limit arcing.

Do not assume every arrest rhythm requires a shock. For an indicated manual shock, continue compressions during charging where safe, minimise interruptions for analysis and shock, and follow the authorised operator or AED pathway.

For oxygen-fire safety, keep free-flow oxygen sources away from the chest and direct ventilator exhaust away from the shock area. Maintain an attached ventilation circuit or bag connected to an advanced airway as appropriate; do not routinely disconnect it solely for defibrillation. Follow the trained resuscitation team's device-specific procedure.
Recognise the arrest, call the team and start chest compressions without delay in line with unit procedure; apply pads as soon as the defibrillator arrives.
Authorised-role requirements for operating a defibrillator apply; follow local policy and training.

The antero-lateral position is the pad/paddle position of choice: the apical (lateral) pad goes below the armpit in the mid-axillary line. If the patient has an implantable pacemaker or defibrillator (ICD), place the pad more than 8 cm away from the device, or use an alternative pad position. Consider an alternative pad position if the patient is prone (bi-axillary) or in a refractory shockable rhythm.
Defibrillator model, pad placement and settings follow the manufacturer's instructions and unit training.
Operation steps and energy selection are not drafted; follow resuscitation training and the device manual per your unit's documentation standard.

Call for help early and follow local oxygen-fire safety rules. Distinguish free-flow oxygen near the chest from an attached closed breathing circuit; trained staff manage the oxygen source and circuit according to the resuscitation and device protocol.

Resume chest compressions immediately after shock delivery. A combination of clinical and physiological signs of return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) - such as return of consciousness, purposeful movement, an arterial waveform, or a sharp rise in end-tidal CO2 - is a reason to consider stopping compressions for a rhythm check, and a pulse check if the rhythm appears appropriate. On a defibrillator that displays the ECG with chest-compression motion artefact removed, the underlying rhythm may guide whether a rhythm and pulse check is needed roughly every two minutes; no pause is needed if asystole is displayed.
Record times, rhythm, shocks and actions on the resuscitation record per unit standard.

checklist.text: Call the team and start compressions without delay per unit procedure.
Apply pads as soon as the defibrillator arrives.
Confirm the authorised rhythm analysis or AED decision indicates a shock; for an indicated manual shock minimise interruptions during charging and delivery.
Call the safety warning and visually confirm everyone is clear of the patient and bed before an indicated shock; never shock during manual compressions.
Check oxygen-fire safety according to the airway circuit and local resuscitation procedure; do not assume all oxygen equipment is handled in the same way.
Record times and actions on the resuscitation record.

Resume CPR immediately after an indicated shock unless the authorised resuscitation team identifies a reason to assess return of circulation; do not stop solely because an isolated capnography value rises.

For oxygen-fire safety, keep free-flow oxygen sources away from the chest and direct ventilator exhaust away from the shock area. Maintain an attached ventilation circuit or bag connected to an advanced airway as appropriate; do not routinely disconnect it solely for defibrillation. Follow the trained resuscitation team's device-specific procedure.

gaps: Energy settings, drug therapy, post-arrest care, cardioversion and children: not covered.
